title: Make check-then-act on shared state atomic

facts.note: Role (PLT-84), mapped to paths by the structure profile.
The task debits or reserves a shared resource.
Diff reads shared state, then writes based on it, with an asynchronous call or other pause in between.

fires: A use case reads a balance, waits on an asynchronous store call, then writes a reduced balance.
A status check happens before a lock or transaction that performs the change.
doesNotFire: State owned by a single request.
A store operation that already performs the conditional update atomically and is used as such.

given: An operation reads shared state and then changes it based on what it read
when: another request for the same aggregate can run between the read and the write
then: Make the read, the decision and the write one atomic unit per aggregate, and re-check every precondition inside that unit.
prefer: A conditional write or transaction in the store when it offers one; otherwise serialise per aggregate key, for example with a keyed lock in the application role.
Keep the critical section to the decision and the write; compute pure inputs outside it.
A test that starts the conflicting operations simultaneously and checks the invariant afterwards.
avoid: A global lock across all aggregates when a per-key one suffices.
Checking preconditions (state, ownership, availability) outside the unit and trusting them inside.
why: Any pause between read and write (an asynchronous call, I/O, a yield) lets two requests act on the same snapshot; tests run sequentially never see it.
evidence: A concurrent test shows the invariant holds (nothing spent twice, no negative balance).
Preconditions are evaluated inside the atomic unit.
